Following my posting of the video link above, a friend asked me to record those Breton tunes again, but this time in the keys they would normally be played in, so here they are.

I’ve played St. Patrick’s An Dro twice in this set, the first time is in the key which Carlos Núñez recorded it in on his LP - Un Galicien En Bretagne & which I prefer, but the 2nd time is in the key more usually heard in sessions.

I’m playing them on English Concertina, Mandolin, Hammered Dulcimer & Fiddle.

Re: St. Patrick’s An Dro=Kas a Barh

This tune is actually a Kas a Barh (See abc below), not an An Dro. An An Dro is a Breton chain/spiral dance done with a pinkie hold, while a Kas a Barh is a couple dance done in a circle of couples, moving clockwise side-by-side holding inside pinkies. They step on beats 1,2,&3, holding on beat 4-a pattern mimicked by the musicians by stomping their feet. The music is similar to but slightly faster and bouncier than an An Dro.
This Kas a Barh is #1821 (of 2365) in Vol 1 of Polig Monjarret’s monumental Toniou Breizh-Izel: Musique Populaire de Basse Bretagne, published in 1913 and now back in print. In common with many of the old Breton tunes, it is simply named after the dance. The mode of C Dorian is how it sounds when played on a Bb bombard/binou pair, but it is actually fingered on Bombard as if it were in Em on a D whistle. The original tune has 4 parts, of which only the first 2 are generally played now.
The 2 modern names listed by others (including “The Caves of King Cintolo”, after a Galician folk tale) were I believe introduced by Carlos Núñez on his 2003 CD “Un Galicien En Bretagne”. I don’t know where he got it. He introduced it to the Cheiftans, who often performed it with him. I twice played this on gaita onstage with Carlos, who would end the first half of his solo shows by getting the audience up to dance an An Dro.

Here is the original version of the tune.

T:Kas a Barh
C:Toniou Breizh Vol 1, #1821
O:(Plenweur, Brittany)
L:1/16
Q:112
M:4/4
N:Key Cdor
